correctness.rationale: The exact two-sided stationary stochastic convolution and conditional variance PDMP are well-defined; the ordinary-time Poisson age gives U=1-(1-a²U′)B with Beta(alpha,1) B independent of U′. For z<1-a² this gives the exact variance-deficit CDF K z^alpha; the stationary polynomial moment identity derives the computable K. A controlled Gaussian mixture Laplace asymptotic yields the far-tail coefficient; the same change of variables gives the Gamma conditional localization. The original process retains bounded conditional Gaussian variance and all absolute moments. All boundary domains, normalizations and fixed-parameter quantifiers have been checked. Standalone recursion, series and conditional-age quadratures executed successfully.

originality.rationale: The physical model of Poisson partial resetting, and the frequent-small-reset diffusion approximation, are known. The accepted distinction is the exact stationary conditional-variance endpoint exponent and computable constant, resulting Gaussian far tail and Gamma localization, and their qualitative mismatch with the approximation. Closest primary sources inspected at model/equation level did not imply those facts; general Laplace asymptotics alone do not determine the model-specific constant.
residual_risks: An implicit derivation may be present in broader Gaussian variance-mixture endpoint asymptotic theory; this comparison was based on primary works found rather than a proof of absolute novelty.
Full generality of existing nonlocal jump-generator/pantograph literature cannot be ruled out by search alone.
The result does not assert a uniform comparison of the diffusion approximation when contraction strength tends to zero jointly with the spatial observation scale.

value.rationale: The exact far-tail exponent and prefactor are natural rare-particle-displacement observables for partially reset particles in an optical/harmonic trap. Their gamma variance localization exposes the atypically long reset-free histories responsible for extremes. The exact all-moments-finite versus algebraic approximate-tail contrast identifies a physically consequential scale at which a frequently used diffusion approximation cannot extrapolate. This is a model-specific sharp asymptotic, not a routine restatement of a known stationary moment.
